output.reasoning:
Offsets, from honest witnesses who checked each timepiece at a known moment: salon clock = true −5 (Vauthier and Odile at ten); kitchen clock = true +15 (Rosa, and Lina at dinner); hall clock = true +12 (Rosa's strike at 11:03 kitchen; Girard's face at 11:02 on return); Girard's watch = true −4; Félix's watch = true −20; Vauthier's watch = +2 at dinner.

Blow time: Félix heard the thump at 10:18 by his watch, which is 10:38 true, and the repeater straight after. Girard heard the repeater bells at 10:34 by his watch, which is 10:38 true. Rule 1 ties the repeater to the blow, so the blow was at 10:38.

Alibis at 10:38: Rosa and Lina were together in the kitchen from 10:22 to 11:00, and each confirms the other. Odile was at the piano from 10:33 to 10:46, heard continuously by Girard, Rosa, Lina and Félix (who heard Chopin during the thump), so she is cleared. Girard was in the street from 10:25 to 10:50 and heard the bells from there. That leaves the upstairs movers: someone went up past the library at 10:35 and came down at 10:41, which Félix reports.

Vauthier's account conflicts with the honest piano timeline. He says he left the salon at 10:43 true (quarter to eleven by his +2 watch), but Odile, Rosa and Girard all place the piano starting at 10:33 true, when Vauthier left. His stated 10:43 would put him in the salon at 10:38. Either he lied, or his watch was altered after dinner, which rule 3 allows only by the murderer's hand. He was in the hall and able to reach the stairs.

Félix's account has an impossibility he cannot escape. He says his uncle came into the library at 10:32 by his watch, which is 10:52 true, and they sat together until eleven. But Monnier was dead at 10:38: the repeater and thump at that moment were the blow, and the slide was still pressed at discovery. Only Félix was in the library to alter his own watch, so this is a false statement by Félix. He also omitted Girard's visit to the library around 10:50. By rule 2, the murderer is the one who lies, and Félix is the only one whose account cannot be reconciled with the true timeline.

The regulator's false 10:05 setting (it read 10:20 when Lina left, after which someone moved the hands back) points at Lina, the only person with Monnier at 10:05. That frame is consistent with a murderer who had access to the atelier after 10:21 and wanted to shift suspicion. The sequence that best fits: Félix went up around 10:35 (the "someone" he reports on the stairs was himself), struck at 10:38, reset the regulator, and came down at 10:41.

Weak point: Vauthier's exit time needs the watch-alteration explanation to be fully consistent. I resolve it by assuming Félix altered Vauthier's watch while Monnier was passing the watches at dinner. That is a plausible reading of the rules, not a proven fact.
